name: What's the difference between MDF and solid wood trim?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between MDF and solid wood trim?

acceptedAnswer.text: MDF (Medium-Density Fiberboard) trim is an engineered wood product, offering a smooth finish ideal for painting and generally more affordable and stable than solid wood, as it resists warping and cracking. Solid wood trim, conversely, is made from natural timber, offering superior durability, the ability to be stained or painted to showcase natural grain, and can be repaired more easily if dented. The choice between them often depends on your budget, desired aesthetic, and the level of wear the trim will experience. For example, solid wood might be preferred for high-traffic areas or historical renovations.
acceptedAnswer.description: MDF is affordable, stable, and good for painting, while solid wood is durable, can be stained, and is better for high-traffic areas.
